summary: Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.
Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. from McGill University, where she became a professor around 1978.

Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Notre Dame, the University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She held positions at Northwestern University and the University of Pennsylvania.

Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher whose appointments include resident scholar at the Bellagio Center (1993), visiting fellow at Australian National University and Canberra School of Music (1997), and professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2012).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist who studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College. She held academic posts at the University of London (~1935–1962), the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl worked in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017) as Associate Professor of Religion.

Kathleen McDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan by 2000, studying under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held attested academic posts at Victoria University of Wellington in 1998 and the University of Manitoba in 1999.

Katia Buffetrille specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald and held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études, Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale, and Études mongoles, sibériennes, centrasiatiques et tibétaines.

Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist. He received his doctorate from Savitribai Phule Pune University and worked at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1970 to 2008, where he was Professor of Geo-archaeology.

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from around 1964 to 1969 and served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2006).
Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Leipzig. He later served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of archaeology and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1893 to 1896 and later held a post there from roughly 1900 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, later serving as a long-time professor at Kyoto University.

Katsumi Okimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor, director, and professor emeritus at Hanazono University between roughly 1986 and 2014.

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1973) and later held positions at Kanazawa University (~1993–1999) and Chuo University (~1999–2011).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist educated at Kyoto University. His career included appointments at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Nara National Museum, Ryukoku University, and Kansai University.
